title: Suggest any good backtesting website
author: ImpressiveEcho3152
selftext: Suggest any no code free backtesting website for Nifty and/or Crypto.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: for Nifty without code, Streak from Zerodha is the one most people end up on, you build the rule from dropdowns and it backtests on Indian stocks and indices. TradingView's built in strategies work too, but changing them means touching Pine.

replies.author: ImpressiveEcho3152
replies.body:
I tried streak, didn't found it too user friendly.
And tradingview uses pine code which I always get wrong🥲

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: Pine going wrong is normal, it has a mean learning curve for something that looks like a spreadsheet. what helped me was writing the rule in plain words first, entry, exit, stop, one line each, and only then handing that to an AI to turn into Pine. the plain words catch half the bugs before any code exists.

replies.author: ImpressiveEcho3152
replies.body: That's a neat trick, will definitely try that. Thanks.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: let me know how it reads once it's down in plain words. that's usually the step where the rule turns out to have a hole in it, before Pine gets a chance to hide it.

replies.author: ImpressiveEcho3152
replies.body: It worked on simple strategy but when the strategy is a bit complex it misses.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: For crypto, Cymetica's Backtest Labs is a no code option where you pick a rule and test it on past data with fees included. For Nifty I'm not sure it covers it, so I'd check which markets it supports. Whatever site you use, look for fees and slippage settings and a way to keep some data aside, because a result without costs usually looks better than it should.

replies.author: ImpressiveEcho3152
replies.body: Does Cymetica supports trsting own strategy or just pre made on their platform?

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: It tests bots on the platform. You can clone one and change its settings, or use your own bot if you have one there. I'm not sure it takes a fully custom rule you write from scratch, so I'd check the page or its docs before counting on that. Correction to what I said earlier, it's more bot based than just picking a rule.
